chunks.title: Anchor a backend summary in service responsibilities
chunks.text: Identify the backend languages and frameworks actually used, the kinds of services or data workloads handled, and a proven reliability or performance outcome. Useful scope includes API traffic, asynchronous jobs, integrations, or data volume. Avoid calling systems scalable or secure without evidence describing how or at what scale.

chunks.title: Separate backend capabilities from tool names
chunks.text: Group languages and frameworks separately from databases, messaging, cloud infrastructure, API protocols, security, testing, and observability. Include concepts such as transactions or caching only if demonstrated. This structure lets reviewers distinguish implementation experience from a long undifferentiated stack list.

chunks.title: Describe backend request and data boundaries
chunks.text: For a backend project, identify the API or event entry point, business-service boundary, persistence layer, external integrations, and asynchronous processing. Explain one design choice such as idempotency, queueing, caching, indexing, or transaction scope. State measured load or failure behavior when it was actually tested.

chunks.title: Replace a vague API bullet with operational evidence
chunks.text: Weak: 'Built scalable REST APIs with Node.js.' Strong: 'Implemented six authenticated order endpoints in Express and added database indexes for the two slowest queries, keeping p95 latency below 250 ms in a 100-request-per-second load test.' Scope and test conditions make the claim auditable.

chunks.title: Prioritize backend keywords that match the vacancy
chunks.text: Common backend concepts include REST or GraphQL APIs, authentication, authorization, SQL, NoSQL, schema design, transactions, caching, message queues, microservices, testing, containers, monitoring, and cloud deployment. Match the job's exact terminology only where the resume contains truthful supporting evidence.

chunks.title: Avoid architecture labels without engineering detail
chunks.text: A list containing microservices, event-driven, secure, cloud-native, and high availability does not show backend competence by itself. Explain service boundaries, events, failure handling, access control, deployment, or monitoring. Do not claim ownership of an organization-wide architecture when the candidate implemented only one component.
